Definition
[local Riemannian isometry]

Source: petersen:page-0213

A map $F:(M,g_M)\to (N,g_N)$ is a local Riemannian isometry if for each $p\in M$, $DF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is a linear isometry. A local coordinate system $\varphi :U\to \Omega \subset \mathbb R^n$, with $U$ given the induced metric $g$ and $\Omega $ the coordinate representation $(\varphi ^{-1})^*g=g_{ij}dx^idx^j$, is a trivial example.
